newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold traders bank on wedding, harvest demand.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold traders bank on wedding, harvest demand.

text.p: Dubai gold traders said on Sunday they were hoping that India's wedding season and an improved harvest there would boost jewellery and bullion sales.

The second Indian marriage season, running from mid-November to the end of February, usually sees a strong upturn in bullion and jewellery purchases, much of which is supplied from Dubai where prices are lower than in Bombay.
"We expect good demand from weddings," one Dubai souk (market) trader said.
"An improved economy (in India) and richer farmers after a better harvest will hopefully bring good results to our business."
He was referring to fiscal reforms implemented by India's Central Bank and expectations of a good harvest after strong monsoon rains between June and September.

Bullion imports into Dubai during this year's first Indian marriage season soared from 27.4 tonnes in March to 32.6 tonnes in April and 33.3 tonnes in May, the highest monthly import figures so far this year.
The Bombay Bullion Association estimates that the number of Indian marriages at 10 million a year, with an average of 30 grams of gold bought for each wedding.

It is wedding demand, after the Diwali (the Hindu festival of lights) holiday earlier this month, that makes India the world's single largest consumer on gold and Dubai a major re-exporter of the yellow metal.
An indicator of Diwali's effect on bullion imports into Dubai should emerge with the release of October import figures later this month by the World Gold Council in Dubai.
Dubai jewellers said Diwali retail businenss in the main 22 carat jewellery sector was up to 15 percent lower than 1995's levels but bullion re-export demand into India remained upbeat.
Imports in September this year were 26.58 tonnes, down from 28.84 tonnes in August and 29.89 tonnes in July, according to figures complied by Dubai customs.

In line with lower international gold prices, Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola (TT bar) -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by Dubai traders on Sunday at 5,204 dirhams ($1,418), down from 5,255 dirhams on November 17.
On the international market, an ounce of gold was last quoted on Saturday at $376.35/85 from the previous Saturday's $380.00/50.
